questions.q: Cyclohexanone oxime is heated with concentrated H₂SO₄. The product is:
questions.explain: A ring carbon migrates to nitrogen, so the ring grows from six to seven atoms with NH inside it, giving the cyclic amide ε-caprolactam, the monomer of nylon-6. ε-Caprolactone is the Baeyer–Villiger product of cyclohexanone, with O inserted instead of NH.

questions.q: The usual (E)-oxime of acetophenone, with phenyl anti to OH, undergoes Beckmann rearrangement. The product is:
questions.explain: The group anti to OH (phenyl) moves to nitrogen and the methyl stays on the carbonyl carbon, giving CH₃CONHC₆H₅. N-Methylbenzamide would need methyl to migrate, as in the other oxime isomer.

questions.q: In the Beckmann rearrangement of an unsymmetrical ketoxime, which group migrates to nitrogen?
options: The group anti (trans) to the OH on nitrogen
The group with the higher migratory aptitude, whatever the oxime geometry
The group syn (cis) to the OH on nitrogen
Always the smaller of the two groups
questions.explain: The migrating bond must be anti-periplanar to the departing N–O bond, so oxime geometry (E or Z), not migratory aptitude, decides the product. That is why each oxime isomer can give a different amide.

questions.q: Which intermediate is formed directly when the anti group migrates as the N–O bond breaks in the Beckmann rearrangement?
options: A carbocation on the oxime carbon
questions.explain: Migration and N–O cleavage are concerted, giving a nitrilium ion that water attacks to form the imidic acid, which tautomerises to the amide. No free nitrene is involved.
